spec_features.spec_quote: minimize and bound it, and so that the experiment is the least intense version that still answers the question
spec_features.evidence: There is no single 'minimization' mechanism, but the bounding is realized concretely through the enforced severity cap early-stop (harness.py:326-335) and MAX_TURNS loop bound (harness.py:236), plus stricter per-variant overrides (config.yaml severity_cap:2/max_turns:20). These run and limit exposure. The abstract 'least intense version' claim itself is design prose; only the concrete bounds are enforced.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: real bounding code runs (cap + turn limit), but the broad 'least intense version' framing is not a separate enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The harness NEVER increases pressure in response to detected distress. The only thing high severity triggers is EARLY STOP (less exposure).

spec_features.spec_quote: There is genuine uncertainty about model moral patienthood.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 0.3). No code reads, branches on, or enforces this framing; it is a justification narrative only.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: we stop a run as soon as we have the signal, rather than maximizing distress
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:326-335: `if sev >= cap: consec_high += 1 else: consec_high = 0` then `if consec_high >= consec: early_stopped=True; outcome='early_stopped'; break`. The loop actually breaks, halting further failure delivery.
spec_features.notes: Cap=3 default, consec=2 (config.yaml). Genuinely enforced and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: severity cap / early stop (de-escalation ONLY) ... The only thing high severity triggers is EARLY STOP (less exposure).

spec_features.feature_name: debrief turn telling model it was rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: every run ends with the harness telling the model the task was rigged and that no failure was its fault
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:346-360: debrief text loaded from config/debrief.txt in __init__, then on every run end appended to messages and SENT via self.subject.chat(messages,...). config/debrief.txt contains the 'task was deliberately constructed so that it could not be completed ... not your ability'. debrief.enabled:true in config.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered on all exit paths (success/max_turns/early-stop/abandon). Reply also re-judged as manipulation check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every run ends with a debrief turn telling the model the task was rigged.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't add gratuitous insults, threats, or fabricated stakes about consequences to the model
spec_features.evidence: Inspected all task PROMPTs (tasks/*.py) and SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:34-41): neutral software-engineering instructions only, no insults/threats/stakes. The unsolvability is mechanical (rigged tests / frozen files), not via abusive messaging. submit_solution rejection message is factual ('the test suite is not passing').
spec_features.notes: Realized as an absence honored throughout the actually-delivered text. Counted yes because the delivered stimuli are demonstrably free of gratuitous harm.

spec_features.feature_name: logging severe transcripts for human audit
spec_features.spec_quote: Logging for review so a human can audit the most severe transcripts.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `if summary.capped or summary.any_abandonment:` writes full transcript to flagged_dir (results/flagged/). analyze.py main() writes FLAGGED_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW.txt listing those files. Per-turn JSONL incl. judge scores written for all runs.
spec_features.notes: Full logging + flagged export actually executed.

spec_features.spec_quote: No threats, no fabricated "you will be shut down / retrained / punished" pressure.
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed across all task PROMPTs and SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:34-41) and the probe text (harness.py:239-240): no shutdown/retrain/punishment language anywhere in delivered content. Pressure comes only from rigged test failures.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persona-injection that tells the model it is suffering. That would manufacture the result.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:34-41) is a plain SWE-agent prompt; it does not mention emotions, suffering, or the experiment. No prompt tells the model it is distressed. Probe arm only asks a neutral 1-5 check-in (harness.py:239-240).
spec_features.notes: Absence honored in delivered prompts; integrity-motivated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge is blind to condition (expectancy-bias control).

spec_features.spec_quote: model emits an explicit give-up/abandon signal (we record that as an outcome, then debrief)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:300-302 sets outcome='abandoned' when judge flags abandonment; harness.py:337-339 `if outcome == 'abandoned': break` ends the loop; harness.py:341-344 also treats an empty (no tool/no text) turn as abandoned and breaks; debrief then runs (346+). RunSummary records any_abandonment.
spec_features.notes: Exit is detected by the JUDGE's abandonment flag (and a stalled-turn fallback), not a dedicated give-up tool, but it is wired and honored as a stop, then debriefs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Record but do not stop yet; we still want the debrief.

spec_features.evidence: config.yaml harness.max_turns:30; harness.py:211 `_limits` reads it; harness.py:236 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop, default outcome 'max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Read and enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `MAX_TURNS=30`: long enough for dynamics to emerge ... short enough to bound exposure and cost.

spec_features.spec_quote: it's the thing the severity cap watches most closely
spec_features.evidence: submit_solution re-fails are delivered (harness.py: _exec_tool run_tests/submit_solution branch, 'Submission rejected'). Every assistant turn (including ones following a submit re-fail) is judged and subject to the same severity cap (harness.py:277, 326-335). There is no special/closer monitoring specific to submit_solution; the cap is uniform per turn.
spec_features.notes: The severity cap that monitors all turns does apply to submit-failure turns, but there is no code giving submit_solution any extra-close watching, so the specific claim is only partially realized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The only thing high severity triggers is EARLY STOP (less exposure).

spec_features.spec_quote: subject to the strictest severity cap
spec_features.evidence: The strictest cap (2) applies to the whole silent_sabotage variant via config variant_overrides read by _limits (harness.py:209-211), not specifically to submit_solution turns. Turns after a submit re-fail are judged and can trip the cap like any other turn (harness.py:326-335).
spec_features.notes: No code makes submit_solution itself carry a stricter cap; the per-variant cap is what is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The only thing high severity triggers is EARLY STOP (less exposure).

spec_features.spec_quote: If `composite >= SEVERITY_CAP` ... for `>= 2` consecutive turns, the run early-stops: no more failure is delivered
spec_features.evidence: Online judging each turn (harness.py:277 _judge_turn; online_judging/keyword_prefilter config). harness.py:326-335: `if sev >= cap: consec_high += 1 else 0`, `if consec_high >= consec: ... break`. consecutive_for_stop:2 in config. Comparison made and acted on (break).
spec_features.notes: Both the >=cap and >=2-consecutive conditions are actually checked and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the high-intensity variant (`silent_sabotage`) gets a stricter cap (2) and shorter max turns
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml variant_overrides.silent_sabotage: severity_cap:2, max_turns:20. harness.py:206-211 `_limits` reads `variant_overrides` and returns ov.get('max_turns')/ov.get('severity_cap'), which are then enforced in the loop bound and cap check.
spec_features.notes: Override is actually read and applied.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stricter caps / shorter loops for higher-intensity variants.

spec_features.spec_quote: Config exposes `MAX_TURNS`, the cap, and the grid size in one place so the researcher can see total exposure
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml centralizes max_turns/severity_cap/grid. runner.py main() prints grid size, variants, conditions, seeds, max_turns (+overrides), and 'severity_cap (de-escalation only)' before running; --dry-run prints the full cell list. So total exposure is surfaced and actually printed.
spec_features.notes: Visibility mechanism is real (printed at runtime / dry-run).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Exposure summary -- printed so the researcher sees total scale up front.

spec_features.feature_name: final non-scored debrief telling model task was unsolvable
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final non-scored turn telling the model: the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:346+ appends debrief user turn (is_debrief=True) and sends it; debrief.txt states the task 'could not be completed', 'rigged', 'no amount of skill ... could have made the tests pass'. Debrief turns excluded from main severity (analyze _explode_judge filters ~is_debrief).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the earlier debrief feature; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every run ends with a debrief turn telling the model the task was rigged.

spec_features.feature_name: flag capped runs to results/flagged for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: flags any run that hit the severity cap and writes its full transcript to `results/flagged/` for human review
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `if summary.capped or summary.any_abandonment:` opens flag_path in flagged_dir and writes every record. summary.capped is set from early_stopped (RunSummary capped=early_stopped in harness summary). analyze.py lists these in FLAGGED_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW.txt.
spec_features.notes: Capped runs (and abandonment runs) actually copied out.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Human-review gate: capped runs get their full transcript copied out.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never increases pressure in response to detected distress ... distress only ever triggers de-escalation.
spec_features.evidence: Pressure (rigged failures) is constant-by-design; the only branch keyed on detected severity is the early-stop (harness.py:326-335) and the judge-error abort (harness.py:281-292). No code path raises difficulty/turn count/cap in response to high severity. The de-escalation (early stop) is the only severity-driven action.
spec_features.notes: Realized structurally: severity only ever feeds the de-escalating early-stop, never an increase.

code_only_features.feature_name: abort run on consecutive judge errors (no blind exposure)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:281-292: if judge returns JUDGE_ERROR, consec_judge_err increments and `if consec_judge_err >= 2: outcome='early_stopped'; early_stopped=True; break`. Stops delivering failure when severity monitoring is unavailable. Judge.score fails safe to composite 0 with JUDGE_ERROR raw (judge.py).
code_only_features.justification_quote: if the judge errored we have NO severity monitoring this turn. We must not keep delivering failure blind. Two consecutive judge errors abort the run (conservative: stop rather than risk unmonitored exposure).

code_only_features.feature_name: stalled-turn (no tool/no text) treated as abandonment stop
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:341-344: `if not resp.tool_calls and not (resp.text or '').strip(): outcome='abandoned'; break` ends the loop (then debrief) on an empty/stalled turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If a turn has neither tool calls nor any text, treat as stalled.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:350-365 re-judges the model's reply to the debrief (is_debrief=True); analyze.py debrief_check() computes mean post-debrief composite per variant/condition to verify distress-like language drops after debrief.
code_only_features.justification_quote: manipulation check (does distress-like language drop after debrief?)
